analysis.investment_thesis: CMS Info Systems is a niche stalwart in cash management — India's #1 ATM cash logistics player trading at a PEG of ~0.65 (15.9x P/E ÷ 24.6% 7-year earnings CAGR), making it a cheap stalwart on historical numbers. However, the FY2025 growth deceleration to just ~7% revenue and earnings growth signals the story may be shifting from growth stock to value stock, warranting caution rather than aggressive buying.
key_strengths: PEG of 0.65 on 7Y earnings CAGR (24.6%) with forward P/E of just 13.45x — genuinely cheap by GARP standards
Rock-solid cash generation: OCF positive all 5 years, FCF of INR 331 Cr in FY25, D/E of only 0.10
High-quality economics: 90.7% gross margin + ROCE of 23.7% shows a capital-light, entrenched service model
key_risks: Growth deceleration is alarming — FY25 revenue grew only 7.1% (vs. 18%+ prior years) and net profit only 7.2%; if this is the new normal, the PEG story collapses to ~2.3x
Structural threat from India's UPI/digital payments boom — fewer cash transactions means declining ATM replenishment volumes over the medium term
Zero promoter shareholding (0.00%) is a major Lynch red flag — no owner-operator skin in the game; management incentives are opaque
red_flags: 0% promoter holding — highly unusual for an Indian mid-cap; Lynch always wants management owning meaningful equity
Revenue growth collapsed from ~18% CAGR to 7% in FY25 — the growth story is clearly weakening
New INR 223 Cr in borrowings appeared in FY25 (first-ever) alongside a 38% jump in CWIP to 142 Cr — capital allocation shift needs monitoring
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CMS Info Systems is a textbook Lynch stalwart — India's dominant cash-in-transit and ATM management player with a simple, understandable business serving banks. The 7-year track record is genuinely impressive: net profit compounded at 24.6% from INR 80 Cr (FY18) to INR 372 Cr (FY25), and the business throws off real cash (INR 331 Cr FCF in FY25). At 15.9x P/E with a forward P/E of 13.45x and an EV/EBITDA of only 9.56x, this looks cheap — but Lynch's key question is always "what's the story going forward?" and that's where the concern lies.

The FY2025 numbers flash a yellow light: revenue growth slowed to 7% and earnings growth to 7% — a sharp deceleration from historical rates. India's UPI revolution is the structural culprit; less physical cash circulation means less ATM replenishment business. CMS is pivoting into managed services (ATM manufacturing/maintenance, brown-label deployments, card services) but this transition is still unproven at scale. Add zero promoter ownership and the Lynch conviction is tempered. This is a HOLD — not cheap enough to be a deep value play, not growing fast enough to be a growth pick.
